newsitem.title: ITALY: Informer says Mafia boss kissed Italy's Andreotti.
newsitem.headline: Informer says Mafia boss kissed Italy's Andreotti.

text.p: Former Italian prime minister Giulio Andreotti heard some of the most incriminating evidence to date at his Mafia trial on Thursday when an informer said he once saw the Mafia's "boss of bosses" kiss him on both cheeks.
Balduccio Di Maggio, a former Mafia boss himself who turned state's evidence, told the court that Godfather Salvatore "Toto" Riina embraced Andreotti during a meeting in Palermo in 1987.

Also present at the meeting was Salvo Lima, a member of the European Parliament who was gunned down in the Sicilian capital in 1992, Di Maggio said. Prosecutors allege Lima was Andreotti's chief political contact in Sicily and his link to the Mafia.
"As soon as Riina and I entered the room, Lima and Andreotti stood up and Riina greeted them with a kiss on the cheeks, one on the right and another on the left," Di Maggio said.
Andreotti, prime minister seven times and for long Italy's most prominent statesman, denies having ties to the Mafia and says the meeting Di Maggio described never took place.
"It's a lie, a tall tale that I've been hearing for three years now," he told reporters during a break in the trial.
As Di Maggio testified, Andreotti, 76, listened impassively, his overcoat thrown over his shoulders to protect from the chill in the fortified courtroom at Rome's Rebibbia prison.
Andreotti's trial, usually held in Palermo, was moved to Rome for security reasons so Di Maggio could testify. He gave his evidence from behind a white screen to shield his face.
Di Maggio, who has spoken of the alleged meeting several times before, has previously described the purported embrace as a Mafioso "kiss of honour".
"I know that Andreotti has denied this episode (the kiss) ever took place, but this is the truth," Di Maggio said.
Di Maggio was Riina's bodyguard and driver. His decision to co-operate with investigators after his arrest was instrumental in the capture of Riina in 1993 after 23 years on the run.

Andreotti is also on trial in the central city of Perugia charged with complicity in the murder of a journalist who was planning to expose the financing of Andreotti's faction of the now-defunct Christian Democrat party. He denies the charge.
